picks.blurb: Iowa State Football vs. UCF Knights: 3 Bold Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Featured Stories Cyclones in the Pros The Iowa State Cyclones are riding some positive momentum into their Week 12 matchup against the UCF Knights. Last weekend, the Cyclones dominated the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium, winning 41-13. That evened their record out at 5-5 on the year, moving them one game away from becoming bowl-eligible. They will look to accomplish that feat on the road against a UCF squad that is also 5-5 on the season, with a marquee victory over the BYU Cougars when they were undefeated and the No. 2 team in the country. How will this Friday night game in Orlando turn out? Here are some bold predictions for the contest. Aiden Flora Held in Check Nov 14, 2026; Ames, Iowa, USA; Iowa State Cyclones running back Aiden Flora (21) strikes the Heisman Pose after scoring against the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Reese Strickland-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. UCF has one of the top-ranked run defenses in the country, coming in at No. 20 in the nation with a run defense grade of 91.2. Finding room is going to be a challenge for a team that ranks near the bottom of the country in run blocking, with the Cyclones earning a woeful 55.1 run-blocking grade. Knowing the success Flora has had, the lack of success in the trenches for the Iowa State offensive line to open lanes is shocking. Flora is going to handle a heavy workload, but he will be held in check as his streak of 175+ yard games will come to an end. But he will still have a solid game with 125 rushing yards. Defense Continues Trending in the Right Direction The Cyclones' defense has been challenged throughout the season, with all of their Power Conference opponents being ranked in the top 80 in points per drive . That streak will continue against the Knights, but Iowa State will have answers for them. An injury to quarterback Alonza Barnett III has kept UCF from truly reaching its potential. Riding some positive momentum after holding Cincinnati to 13 points, Jesse Bobbit's unit will continue that success against the Knights, who don’t excel along the offensive line. The Knights are ranked 108th with a pass-blocking grade of 57.2 and they are 115th in run-blocking with a grade of 54.3. Iowa State isn’t elite as a run defense or pass rush, but they should have an edge in the trenches to take advantage of. The Cyclones will pick up a hard-fought win, 27-21. For a rebuilding year, this has been a blast. UCF was the team that beat BYU right after the giant Cougar win over Notre Dame. It's been up and down, though, with some puzzling clunkers to go along with the five wins. Get this, though, and there's a shot at the program's first winning season since 2022. When things are clicking, the Knights can hang with anyone – like they showed against BYU. But when the defense isn't taking the ball away and the offense isn't finding its up-tempo groove, forget it. Iowa State has only turned the ball over more than once in one game: the loss to Utah. It won't give the ball up, and the offensive balance will be there to finally get the first road win of the year. home.headline: UCF Q&A: How does Lewis Carter’s return help the Knights?
home.blurb: “Lewis, like a lot of our guys, he's been out a long time,” said coach Scott Frost . “He’s going to continue to get better as he gets closer to 100% and shakes the rust off a little bit. He’s a great person and a great player. He’s one of our leaders and we’ve missed him.” Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book This was supposed to be Lewis Carter ‘s breakout season. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. It felt good,” said Carter, who finished with three tackles on 25 snaps. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. We’ve just got to finish those plays. There were at least three the other night when he had free shots and didn’t get the quarterback down.” UCF's offense shines, defense steps up | Five takeaways from Iowa State win Bianchi: Six wins, zero apologies! home.headline: UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury
home.blurb: Throughout the long seven weeks, including the bye, Carter said he kept his head down and attacked recovery. He made progress, and the Frost hinted at an inevitable return since Oct. 26. UCF's coach said the senior was a game-time decision before the Oct. 30 matchup against the Baylor Bears, and if not, he'd be a game-time decision on the road against the Kansas Jayhawks. Carter didn't return in either. However, Frost's optimism about his availability was a positive sign that the Knights' defense would get their captain back. UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:36 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Lewis Carter missed six straight conference games before returning in the UCF Knights ' 26-13 loss to the Arizona State Sun Devils last Saturday. Carter sustained a knee injury in Week 3 against the Georgia State Panthers, as fans and media saw him enter the medical tent. Coach Scott Frost said he was unaware his senior was injured, and it spiraled into missing the star linebacker. Their captain made his conference debut against Arizona State. He had a quiet performance, posting three solo tackles. The star linebacker said he's 100% and wants to put his best foot forward to help his team win. UCF is one win away from a bowl game, snapping a two-year drought. Carter quarterbacks the defense, communicates adjustments when the offense audibles and shores up tackling. He led the team with 92 tackles last season and was on pace to continue wearing the crown until he got injured. UCF sorely missed his presence over the middle, but its depth stepped up. Tackett Curtis is the team's leading tackler with a career-high 67 tackles, two passes defended, two sacks and two interceptions. Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings have contributed alongside Curtis. They tallied 67 tackles, three pass deflections and 1.5 sacks. The Knights' front seven got its best linebacker back during a crucial Friday game against the Cyclones. Frost said they will be a " good challenge " with a dual-threat quarterback and the Big 12's leading rusher. Aiden Flora leads with 1,335 yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. Flora has tallied five 150-plus-yard games and four multi-touchdown games. He rushed for a career-high 221 yards in a 51-49 upset over the then-No. 24 Oklahoma State Cowboys and reached a career-best three touchdowns twice: once in a 45-42 win over the West Virginia Mountaineers and in a 41-13 blowout over the Cincinnati Bearcats. Carter's ability to blow up the run game is what UCF needs to avenge last week's disappointing loss and send him off with one final home win on Senior Knight.

They won to avoid a late-season collapse, giving the fanbase hope and reminding the college football community that they are, in fact, a formidable threat amongst the nation’s best teams. The upside for Ohio State is that a win Saturday against a Cornhuskers team that looked like it was in CFP contention just a month ago will keep the Buckeyes in the mix. But the question remains: how long? Regarding the logjam at the top of the standings, the UCLA Bruins and Indiana Hoosiers can clinch berths in the conference title game as soon as Saturday. Therefore, this means Ohio State could be fighting for an at-large CFP bid. Nonetheless, Ohio State should win this game. The talent gap is too one-sided to call a potential upset a smart pick. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Close Call for Ohio State’s Playoff Hopes Against Nebraska Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Ohio State’s College Football Playoff hopes depend on winning out, and the first step comes Saturday at Nebraska, where ESPN analyst Greg McElroy expects a tight game with a true freshman under center for the Buckeyes. The 7-3 Buckeyes climbed six spots to No. 14 in Tuesday’s playoff rankings , just outside the top 12. On his Always College Football podcast, McElroy noted Ohio State has “ lost two of the last three ” since quarterback Julian Sayin hurt his right arm at Indiana. What does Ohio State need? IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ohio State’s path is simple but unforgiving. The Buckeyes have to beat Nebraska and Michigan and hope the committee rewards a résumé built on road wins at Indiana and Iowa. Two of Ohio State’s three losses, to USC and Oregon, came after Sayin went down. Ohio State coach Ryan Day has been planning to play without Sayin through the postseason , and he admitted the Buckeyes are still rebuilding. “When you lose two weeks in a row, you don’t have any momentum , so you have to build it,” Day said Tuesday. Day called Fahey “pretty unflappable” but made it clear this week is a step up. “I think he’s learned from each game, but he still hasn’t played a whole lot of football, and so this is the next challenge for him to go win a game on the road ,” Day said. Lincoln is a tough place for that test. McElroy pointed out that opponents convert just under 24% of their third downs against Nebraska. The Huskers are also tied for third nationally in third- and fourth-down success rate allowed . McElroy didn’t spare the Buckeyes’ front either. “The offensive line just doesn’t move anybody off the ball,” he said, adding that Ohio State averages 4.1 yards per carry. That puts more of the load on Jeremiah Smith, the Heisman Trophy betting favorite with 1,317 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns. However, McElroy warned that a pass-heavy game plan is a bad sign for Ohio State. “When Ryan Day’s team throws it 40 or more times, he’s just 5-5,” he said. Can Nebraska pull the upset? IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nebraska opened 5-0, then lost four straight, three of them by seven points or fewer. The Huskers ended the skid with a 31-0 win at Rutgers that clinched bowl eligibility. Injuries have made this week harder. McElroy named cornerback Andrew Marshall as a key piece against Smith, but Nebraska coach Matt Rhule confirmed Monday that Marshall is done for the year after surgery for a stress fracture. Defensive tackle Jahsear Whittington, who leads the team with six sacks, left the Rutgers win with an apparent knee injury. “One of the main things from that game to take away is just the amount of guys that stepped up with injuries ,” Rhule said. Nebraska’s kicking is another worry, since the Huskers are 6 of 13 on field goals. McElroy said that when a drive stalls, “it’s a coin flip on whether or not they walk out with points.” McElroy picks Ohio State to win 19-17. “I do, however, think that Nebraska will make a mistake or two, which ultimately gives Ohio State the victory,” he said. A two-point win would keep the Buckeyes alive, but it wouldn’t do much to impress a committee that had them at No. 20 a week ago. Ohio State and Nebraska kick off at noon ET Saturday on Fox. Ohio State vs. Nebraska Prediction Ohio State Buckeyes Quarterback Luke Fahey continues to lead Ohio State through a top Big Ten ranking in scoring and total offense. The freshman signal-caller played his first clean game from a turnover-worthy play perspective against Northwestern , connecting for 201 passing yards and three touchdown s. There has been no shortage of targets for Heisman contender Jeremiah Smith , generating a season-high 17 targets against the Wildcats . Smith continues to build a case as the best player in college football, and he's now up to 15 touchdowns and an elite four yards per route run on the season. While Fahey has seen 37 pressures in three starts under center, the defense has failed to create pressure. Ohio State has just 16 sacks on the season after an outburst of five against Northwestern. Despite a low amount of pressure for coordinator Matt Patricia, the defense has been one of the best in the country at stopping the rush, dominating offenses that elect to use zone read with a 50% Success Rate . Passing downs have not been friendly to Ohio State, though, ranking outside the top 100 in EPA allowed alongside a third-down conversion allowed rank of 86th. Nebraska Cornhuskers Head coach Matt Rhule shook up the offense after four consecutive losses, firing coordinator Dana Holgorsen. Nebraska scored a grand total of 23 points in the second half of all four losses . The Cornhuskers responded with a 31-0 victory over Rutgers , a road trip that included 17 points in the second half. The top advantage for Nebraska has been the ability to create explosive plays on the ground, ranking sixth in Rush EPA. Quarterback Anthony Colandrea leads the team in 10-yard gains with 22, while running back Jamal Rule's elusiveness has forced 25 missed tackles and 4.7 yards after first contact. Coordinator Rob Aurich has created a menacing Cornhusker defense that has allowed less than 15 points a game with top-35 ranks in Success Rate allowed and Methodical Drives allowed. The defense has shut down opposing passing attacks from creating explosives, ranking fifth in EPA allowed. The pass rush is led by edge Williams Nwaneri and interior Jahsear Whittington, both providing 20 pressures apiece. The rush defense has taken the largest step forward, as Nebraska ranks 20th in Line Yards compared to a number outside the top 100 a year ago. More than 70% of the running back's rushing attempts come through zone read. Ohio State prefers to run inside zone with 11 personnel while using a two-tight end set for outside zone. The Cornhusker defense has respectable numbers against inside zone at a 55% Success Rate, creating a higher number of 58% against opponents using 12 personnel with outside zone . The game for Nebraska's offense will be decided in counter concepts, generating an explosive on 22% of its 77 rushing attempts. picks.headline: Nebraska vs. Ohio State Odds: Can the Huskers Overcome the Buckeyes in Final Home Game of 2026?
picks.blurb: Nebraska vs. Ohio State Odds: Can the Huskers Overcome the Buckeyes in Final Home Game of 2026? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates PISCATAWAY, NJ - NOVEMBER 14: Luke Lindenmeyer #8 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:22 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Well, would you look at that? Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

picks.headline: ESPN predicts winner of Ohio State football vs Nebraska Saturday
picks.blurb: ESPN predicts winner of Ohio State football vs Nebraska Saturday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates ESPN predicts winner of Ohio State football vs Nebraska Saturday Phil Harrison, Buckeyes Wire · Buckeyes Wire Wed, November 18, 2026 at 7:37 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ohio State's first two games without Julian Sayin as starting quarterback were far from what anyone expected. The Buckeyes looked unprepared, sloppy, and undisciplined en route to a 30-18 loss in L.A., and followed that up with an u ninspiring beatdown at the hands of Oregon in Columbus to the tune of 41-28. However, the Buckeyes bounced back last week and took down Northwestern 28-19 to get back on track. Next up is a road trip to Nebraska before things close out at home vs. -- ahem, you know -- Michigan . And now, thanks to the latest College Football Playoff rankings, it sure feels like Ohio State is in the mix to get into the playoff if it wins out and gets a little help. In fact, Ohio State checked in at No. 14 in the third release of the rankings just released on Tuesday, and that's six spots higher already than the week prior and just three spots away from making the 12-team field. According to the analytics ESPN uses to predict the chances of victory, Ohio State has a 71.3% chance of beating the Cornhuskers . That's good and fine, but we have to remember that this same model had the Buckeyes with a significant chance of beating the Trojans on the road, and then the Ducks at home, and neither of those turned out so well. Hopefully, the worldwide leader has this one right just like last week, and we can be celebrating a much-needed win to set up a matchup against Michigan that could be bigger than we thought just a couple of weeks ago. Since these analytics are updated by game results only, there's no chance of this percentage changing, but the Buckeyes will still need to execute at a high level, help out freshman quarterback Luke Fahey , and not make as many mental mistakes, especially on the road. The game is set to kick off at Noon ET on Fox, and we'll have more on the game leading up to Saturday, and be around during and after as well for extensive coverage. Hopefully, we are setting the stage for "The Game" with some things on the line. away.headline: Ohio State football offensive lineman ruled out vs. Nebraska
away.source: The Plain Dealer Cleveland on MSN
away.blurb: LINCOLN, Neb. — Ohio State football’s Phillip Daniels will be sidelined Saturday against Nebraska, as the right tackle was deemed out on the Buckeyes’ pregame injury report. Daniels has not played since a Nov. 7 loss to Oregon. During last week’s win against Northwestern, Daniels was a game-time decision. He was in uniform but did not play. With Daniels out, Ohio State will likely start Austin Siereveld at left tackle, Luke Montgomery at left guard, Carson Hinzman at center and Ian Moore at right tackle. It’s unclear who will start at right guard, as Jake Cook and Gabe VanSickle are likely to battle for the spot. Ohio State will also be without quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, offensive lineman Max Riley, tight end Max LeBlanc, defensive back Brenten “Inky” Jones and safety Terry Moore. Nebraska will be without notable pieces on defense, including linebacker Owen Chambliss, defensive lineman Jahsear Whittington and defensive back Andrew Marshall. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. picks.blurb: Purdue football Wisconsin scouting report, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Story by Journal & Courier Purdue football Wisconsin scouting report, prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads WEST LAFAYETTE − For Purdue football fans, it's a memory stained in their memory. The undefeated fifth-ranked Boilermakers led No. 10 Wisconsin 17-14 in a nationally televised game (back when that wasn't the norm) and with ESPN College Gameday set up on campus. Kyle Orton ran a naked bootleg on third down, seemingly keeping the drive alive for Purdue to burn more clock, only Orton was hit, jarring the ball loose. Scott Starks picked it up and returned it 40 yards for a touchdown. After Bernard Pollard blocked the extra point, the Boilers drove into field goal range but missed a game-tying field goal attempt in the final minute. Wisconsin escaped Ross-Ade Stadium with a 20-17 victory , its first in what is now a string of 18 consecutive Badger victories in the series. On Saturday, Purdue coach Barry Odom gets his first chance to end more than two decades of coming up on the wrong side against the Badgers . Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images (Jeffrey Becker, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 7 Purdue football visits Iowa in primetime | Top photos from the game Purdue football visits Iowa in primetime | Top photos from the game "I was in high school the last time Purdue beat Wisconsin in Ross-Ade and then I am aware that they've won 18 straight," Odom said. "The great thing is this team had nothing to do with that. But it is history. I What to knthink you always learn from those things. You take those things and use it as needed or as you think your current team needs." Odom's timeframe is off. He was a sophomore linebacker at Missouri when Purdue defeated Wisconsin 45-20 at Ross-Ade Stadium in 1997, but his point was made. It's been a long time. What to know about Purdue football's opponent, Wisconsin The Badgers are 6-4, coming off a loss to Maryland in what has been an up-and-down season that includes a 24-7 win over USC on Oct. 24. Wisconsin allows just 17 points per game, problematic for a Purdue offense that has both looked phenomenal and, more recently, shown an inability to capitalize in the red zone. Wisconsin is allowing just 2.8 yards per carry this season, aided by the Badgers' 20 sacks. Oct 16, 2026; West Lafayette, Indiana, USA; Washington Huskies linebacker Taariq al-Uqdah (0) is tackled by Purdue Boilermakers linebacker Jojo Hayden (0) during the second half at Ross-Ade Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images What is undetermined is who'll line up behind center against Purdue. Quarterback Ryan Hopkins was injured on a strip sack late in a loss on Nov. 14 against Maryland, setting up the Terrapins' game-winning field goal. Hopkins is listed as questionable entering Saturday's game. Hopkins was elevated to starting quarterback to replace the struggling Colton Joseph two weeks ago. WISCONSIN STATISTICAL LEADERS − Passing: Colton Joseph (106-189, 1,368 yards, 11 TD, 5 INT), Ryan Hopkins (37-59, 411 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT). Rushing: Abu Sama III (68 car., 373 yards, 1 TD), Joseph (91 car., 371 yards, 4 TD). Receiving: Tyrell Henry (36 rec., 434 yards, 1 TD), Jacob Harris (20 rec., 347 yards, 4 TD). Tackles: Cooper Catalano (100), Mason Posa (86). Tackles for loss: Sebastian Cheeks (9), Posa (7.5). Sacks: Cheeks (7). Interceptions: Marvin Burks Jr. (2). Kicking: Gavin Lahm (15-17 FG, long of 51). Punting: Sean West (39 punts, 43.3 average). Purdue football players to watch Antonio Harris began the season as Purdue's fourth running back. Meanwhile, he became a special teams standout while also slowly working his way up the running back depth chart. During Purdue's four-game losing streak, Harris is averaging 10.1 yards per carry, but has only taken 15 handoffs. For the season, Harris leads Purdue with 6.8 yards per carry and has not had a negative yardage run. With Fame Ijeboi not producing at the clip he had earlier in the season, offensive coordinator Josh Henson could lean more on the flourishing Harris to revive a struggling rushing attack. Despite falling behind early at Iowa, Purdue's defense finally showed some semblance of a pass rush in its first week without Kevin Kane leading the defense. Keyshawn Burgos had a breakout performance with three tackles, a sack and a blocked field goal. Will the Virginia Tech transfer's productivity carry over against Wisconsin? PURDUE STATISTICAL LEADERS − Passing: Ryan Browne (193-311, 2,418 yards, 12 TD, 6 INT). Rushing: Fame Ijeboi (175 car., 684 yards, 10 TD), Antonio Harris (38 car., 242 yards, 2 TD). Receiving: Asaad Waseem (49 rec., 802 yards, 1 TD), Xavier Townsend (44 rec., 477 yards, 3 TD). Tackles: Jojo Hayden (77), Charles Correa (68), Justin Denson Jr. (66). Tackles for loss: Correa (5), Jeremy Lewis (3.5). Sacks: Curt Neal (2.5), Keyshawn Burgos (2.5). Interceptions: Jojo Hayden (2). Kicking: Jacobo Echeverria Lozano (21-23 FG, long of 49, 27-27 PAT). Punting: Dylan Drennan (39 punts, 44.8 average). What uniform combination will Purdue wear vs. Wisconsin Purdue will wear black helmets with black jerseys and gold pants against Wisconsin. Purdue football honorary captain vs. Wisconsin Former Purdue quarterback Joey Elliott will serve as honorary captain against the Badgers. Elliott currently works in the Indianapolis Colts front office as assistant director of pro scouting. Elliott played for Purdue from 2006-09. In 2009 as a senior, Elliott threw for 3,026 yards and 22 touchdowns. Purdue football vs. Wisconsin prediction In a season where nothing makes sense, from the defensive coordinator hire to going to the wire against Wake Forest and UCLA (far more impressive now than it seemed then) to two surprising wins followed by a couple surprising losses, it's only fitting this would be the year this 18-game losing streak to the Badgers ends. Prediction: Purdue 24, Wisconsin 20 Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. away.blurb: With two games to play in the regular season, however, that luck may be running out . Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. away.blurb: Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3) suffered a frustrating 24-21 loss Saturday at Maryland (4-6, 2-5), a result that only intensified questions surrounding the program's direction . Having already handed out grades for the offense , Badgers On SI now breaks down the defense and special teams. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. home.headline: Wisconsin football gets bad news on Javan Robinson, O-line from initial Purdue injury report
home.blurb: With two games to play in the regular season, however, that luck may be running out . Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. Wisconsin Football is Running Out of Time to Fix its Ground Game Other than the constant shuffling on the offensive line, much of which was caused at least initially by injuries suffered before the season began, Wisconsin football has had a relatively clean bill of health for much of the year, especially considering head coach Luke Fickell's past injury luck in Madison. When Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 B1G) travels to face Purdue (3-7, 2-5 B1G) on Saturday afternoon in West Lafayette, it could be without several key starters in a game that's critically important for Fickell and company to bounce back and win after the late collapse in College Park last weekend. We already knew that starting safety Matt Jung was lost for the season, joining the likes of offensive tackle Kevin Heywood and cornerback Cai Bates. But the Badgers' initial injury report poses more questions than answers ahead of a game against Purdue in which, again, Wisconsin could really use a bounce-back victory on the road. Status of key starters in question vs. Boilermakers That's especially relevant this week, as Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten with 2,418 passing yards. The Boilermakers also have some dangerous wide receivers, although their leading pass-catcher Asaad Waseem is primarily a slot

home.headline: Ryan Hopkins headlines first Wisconsin vs. Purdue availability report
home.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. picks.headline: Matchup Preview and Final Score Prediction for Virginia vs. North Carolina
picks.blurb: Matchup Preview and Final Score Prediction for Virginia vs. North Carolina Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB Virginia and North Carolina have played 130 times. The stakes for the 131st matchup are simple, as both teams are 5-5, and the winner becomes bowl-eligible. However, the loser of Saturday’s matchup will still get one more shot. North Carolina plays 4-6 NC State at home on Nov. 28, and Virginia travels to Blacksburg to face Franklin’s 6-4 Virginia Tech team. Saturday is the easier path for the Cavaliers on Senior Day. Bill Belichick hasn't announced who will play quarterback, and the Tar Heels will be without two of their best defenders for at least part of the afternoon. Why this game matters A win would send Virginia to a bowl game for the second straight season, which hasn't happened since 2018 and 2019. It isn't last year's 11-3 finish, but it would salvage a season that looked like it was slipping away less than a month ago. The Cavaliers lost three straight ACC games in October, bottoming out with a 51-7 blowout loss at Wake Forest. After the bye, they beat Cal 36-7, their largest-margin win in an ACC game under Tony Elliott, but the Hoos haven't won back-to-back games since opening the season against NC State and Norfolk State. "It's extremely important just for the mindset and mentality of our program," Elliott said Tuesday. "We're fortunate to be able to play two more games, right? And it doesn't matter who we play, when we play, where we play, what the circumstances are, what the record is." Homefield advantage could help. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium this season and has won 11 of its last 13 games there since the start of 2025. North Carolina has been the opposite: 1-4 at home and 3-1 on the road, with both of its ACC wins (Pitt and Duke) away from Chapel Hill. A win Saturday would be UNC's fourth straight road win. Recent history in Charlottesville doesn't favor the Hoos, though. UNC won its last two trips to Scott Stadium, 31-28 in 2022 and 41-14 in 2024, and Virginia hasn't beaten the Tar Heels at home since 2020. Elliott is 2-0 against UNC in Chapel Hill and 0-2 against them in Charlottesville. Last year's meeting was the 17-16 overtime win at Kenan Stadium that ended with Benjamin Hall stopped inches short on a two-point try. Virginia will honor about 50 upperclassmen before kickoff. The Cavaliers lead the country with 31 players in at least their fifth year of college, including seventh-year punter Daniel Sparks and kicker Will Bettridge, the program's all-time leading scorer. They arrived on Grounds in 2022, @Coach_TElliott 's first year with @UVAFootball , and each has become an integral part of the program. "The foundation that's been built, they laid it," Elliott says of five-year starters @Dsparks115 and @will_bettridge . https://t.co/2qUwjvTice Who's playing quarterback for North Carolina? Billy Edwards Jr. has taken the first snap in all 10 of UNC's games. He left last week's 16-14 loss to Louisville in the third quarter with what UNC's own game recap called an apparent upper-body injury, and he was still listed as questionable on Thursday night's availability report. Belichick has said UNC is taking Edwards' status day by day, and earlier in the week, he said Edwards was "getting better," according to WRAL. He hasn't named a starter, and the ACC's final availability report isn't due until two hours before kickoff. Edwards has completed 65.5% of his passes for 2,247 yards, 18 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He's a pocket passer. Counting sacks, he has zero net rushing yards on 51 carries. His best game came against then-No. 1 Miami, when he went 28 of 34 for 341 yards and four touchdowns in a 38-35 loss. If he can't go, it's likely Travis Burgess. The true freshman made his college debut against Louisville and went 6 of 11 for 59 yards with an interception. He also ran eight times for 35 yards, and UNC's game notes point out that he gained 52 yards on his five non-sack carries, four of which picked up first downs. If he starts, he'd be the first true freshman to start at quarterback for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019, according to the Fayetteville Observer. Belichick said Monday that UNC will have "the same offense" either way, though some plays get more emphasis with one quarterback than the other. Virginia's pass defense has carried this unit, but the run defense has been weaker. Opponents average 4.2 yards per carry against UVA, and 17 of the 25 touchdowns Virginia has allowed have come on the ground. The worst of it came at Florida State, where quarterback Ashton Daniels ran for five touchdowns in a 38-7 Seminoles win. North Carolina's run game hasn't scared many people this year. The Tar Heels average 114.2 rushing yards per game and 3.7 yards per carry. A quarterback who can pick up a third down with his legs changes that, and it would hand defensive coordinator John Rudzinski a different set of problems than Edwards does. Jelani Thurman vs. a thin linebacker room UNC will be looking for the same two targets. Receiver Jordan Shipp leads the Tar Heels with 57 catches for 703 yards. Tight end Jelani Thurman has 50 catches for 597 yards, and his eight touchdown catches tie the UNC single-season record for a tight end and lead all tight ends nationally. The 6-foot-6 Mackey Award semifinalist has at least three catches in every game this season and a team-high 328 yards after the catch. On paper, Virginia is built to handle a passing offense. The Cavaliers lead the ACC in pass defense (186.6 yards per game) and pass efficiency defense, and they've allowed only eight passing touchdowns all year. They also have 11 interceptions, including three against Cal. Two of those went back for touchdowns: Brandyn Hillman's 100-yard return and Kam Robinson's 33-yarder. The question is who covers the middle of the field. Linebacker Maddox Marcellus is out for the season after knee surgery, and fellow linebacker Landon Danley is also listed as out this week. Marcellus had 44 tackles and 4.5 tackles for loss in nine games. Danley has 29 tackles and two starts. Justin Rowe got the start in Marcellus' spot against Cal, the first of his career. He has 12 tackles this season and returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown against Delaware. Myles Brown has played in all 10 games and has 34 tackles and three pass breakups, but he hasn't started a game this year. That's a lot to put on two backups against a tight end who is this good with the ball in his hands. Robinson (46 tackles, six tackles for loss, two interceptions) will need to be at his best in the middle, and Virginia at least has its safeties back. Hillman and Ethan Minter both returned from injuries against Cal. If Thurman has a big day, UNC can move the ball even without much of a running game. If Virginia's linebackers hold up, the Tar Heels have to find another way to beat the ACC's top pass defense. Can Virginia finish drives in the end zone? Virginia's defense has played well enough to win most weeks. The offense is definitely the bigger unknown, and the problems show up after it crosses the 20-yard line. UVA has scored touchdowns on 22 of 37 red zone trips (59%) and converted 43 of 136 third downs (32%). It has also gone for it on fourth down 34 times, converting 22. Even the Cal win followed the pattern. Virginia is 0-4 when it scores fewer than 21 points and 5-1 when it scores 21 or more. The passing game has narrowed since the start of the season. Pribula hasn't thrown more than one touchdown pass in a game since Sept. 26 against Delaware, and his last four have all gone to Da'Shawn Martin, who has seven touchdown catches this season. North Carolina's defense also gives up plenty on third down, as opponents convert 44% of the time, but it tightens up near the goal line. Teams have scored touchdowns on just 18 of 34 red zone trips against the Tar Heels (53%). Elliott liked what he saw from his line against Cal. "I thought [we] dominated the line of scrimmage. ... So, I thought there was a lot of progress," he said Tuesday. "I thought the quarterback came out clean, didn't get hit much." That will be harder to repeat against Xavier Lewis. The sophomore defensive tackle has 44 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and seven sacks, and he's a Bednarik Award semifinalist, the first Tar Heel to make that list since Julius Peppers in 2001. Virginia has allowed 28 sacks this season, and its interior line is in flux. Center Drake Metcalf is questionable, and against Cal, Noah Josey moved from left guard to center with Ben York starting at left guard. UNC will be without the other half of its pass rush. Defensive end Melkart Abou Jaoude, who had three sacks in last year's game, is out with a broken right hand. He has two sacks and a team-high nine quarterback hurries this season. The run game is Virginia's best way to stay ahead of the chains. UNC allows 4.0 yards per carry and 149.6 rushing yards per game, and the Cavaliers ran for 201 yards against Cal. Jekail Middlebrook (540 yards, 4.9 per carry) is listed as the starter after missing the Wake Forest game and getting a light workload on the ground against Cal. Solomon Beebe has also started to see more of the ball. "He probably has the most juice of all the [running backs], he's got the home run potential," Elliott said of Beebe. Turnovers and field position If this game turns into the low-scoring battle the betting totals suggest, the difference will likely come down to two areas where Virginia has an edge. The first is turnovers. Virginia has given the ball away six times all season (three interceptions, three lost fumbles), tied for seventh-fewest nationally. The Cavaliers have forced 12 turnovers and outscored opponents 45-9 in points off turnovers. North Carolina is -3 in turnover margin. The Tar Heels have lost seven of their eight fumbles, and they're 0-4 in games where they haven't forced a turnover. Safety Greg Smith III, who has a team-high three interceptions, will sit out the first half after the ACC suspended him for his role in the postgame fight against Louisville. The first quarter has been Virginia's best this season, outscoring opponents 79-34, so the first 15 minutes could be an opportunity to take some big shots. The second edge is the punting game. Sparks is a true X-Factor as he leads the nation at 50.6 yards per punt, and 21 of his 43 punts have pinned opponents inside the 20. Even after returns, Virginia nets 42.8 yards per punt to UNC's 38.1. In a game where both offenses could have trouble finishing drives, a few extra yards on every exchange add up. UNC does have a weapon in the return game. Freshman Jaden Jefferson took a kickoff 98 yards for a touchdown against ranked Notre Dame on his first college touch. TV: The CW (Thom Brennaman, Jason Cabinda and Wes Bryant) Time: 12:30 p.m. ET Saturday Location: Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, Va. Radio: Virginia Sports Radio Network (John Freeman, Ahmad Hawkins and Jay James); SiriusXM 175 or 234 FanDuel Sportsbook opened Virginia as a 1.5-point favorite with an over/under of 43.5, and neither number had moved as of Friday afternoon. FanDuel has Virginia at -120 on the moneyline and North Carolina at even money (+100), so the market sees the Hoos as only a slight home favorite. The next chance comes in the latest edition of "The South's Oldest Rivalry" as the Tar Heels (5-5, 2-4 ACC) travel to Virginia (5-5, 3-4) for an ACC game at Scott Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21. Kickoff is set for 12:30 p.m. and the game will be televised on The CW . Watch UNC-Virginia on Fubo BOWL PROJECTIONS: Will UNC football make postseason? Latest bowl projections before Virginia game INJURY REPORT: Who is on UNC football vs Virginia injury report? Latest from ACC availability report POSTGAME BRAWL: ACC announces suspensions, fines for UNC football and Louisville after postgame fight UNC has a 4-1 record away from Chapel Hill this season, including a season-opening win against TCU in Ireland. The Tar Heels have won three straight road games since a mid-September loss at Clemson. UNC has also won consecutive games on Virginia's home field. If it stretches that streak to three, it would be the first time since 2016. Overall, the Tar Heels have a 28-27 record at Virginia. Here are some stats to know, players to watch and a score prediction for the Tar Heels vs. Cavaliers. Billy Edwards or Travis Burgess as UNC quarterback vs Virginia? Who will be UNC's starting quarterback vs. Virginia? That's the biggest question surrounding this game. A sixth-year player who started the first 10 games of the season, Billy Edwards Jr. was listed as questionable on the initial ACC availability report . That could open the door for freshman QB Travis Burgess to get his first career start. Burgess replaced Edwards in the second half of the Tar Heels' loss to Louisville, leading a late scoring drive that gave UNC an opportunity to win in the fourth quarter. If Burgess does get the start, he would be the first true freshman to start at QB for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019. UNC defense faces challenge vs Virginia QB Beau Pribula without Greg Smith UNC's defense is arguably coming off its best performance of the season, limiting a Louisville offense that averaged more than 40 points per game to 16 at Kenan Stadium. The Tar Heels won't face that level of explosiveness against Virginia, but it could be tough because of the absence of two key players. Defensive back Greg Smith and defensive lineman Melkart Abou Jaoude are among the Tar Heels out vs. the Cavaliers, but Smith is only out for the first half for his role in the postgame brawl vs. Louisville. In Virginia's wins, quarterback Beau Pribula is averaging 171 passing yards and 45 rushing yards with 11 passing TDs, one rushing TD and one interception. In five losses, Pribula is averaging 174 passing yards and 7 rushing yards with four passing TDs, two interceptions and a rushing TD. If UNC can bottle up Pribula, it'll likely leave Charlottesville its sixth win of the season. UNC running back Benjamin Hall gets redemption shot vs Virginia Benjamin Hall was just short of the goal line on a two-point conversion that would have given UNC its first signature win under Bill Belichick in 2025. The Tar Heels lost 17-16 to No. 16 Virginia in overtime last season at Kenan Stadium . With three touchdowns in the last two weeks, including a two-TD effort vs. Louisville, Hall will have a chance at redemption on Saturday at Scott Stadium. The junior running back's two best games of the season came on the road. Hall logged 130 rushing yards and a receiving TD at Clemson and racked up 81 rushing yards and a TD on nine carries at UConn. UNC vs Virginia score prediction UNC 22, Virginia 18: The Tar Heels have been a different team on the road this season, finding ways to win by creating takeaways and scoring on explosive plays. Even with its questions at QB, UNC seems to get a jolt away from Chapel Hill. Belichick's boys will be celebrating in Charlottesville after securing bowl eligibility ahead of the regular-season finale. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect North Carolina vs Virginia Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo North Carolina Tar Heels Virginia Cavaliers Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, VA Saturday, November 21, 2026 Ron Romanelli Big Al McMordie See the full rankings: Best College Football Handicappers North Carolina Tar Heels vs. Virginia Cavaliers Prediction I'm taking North Carolina and the points against Virginia. Both teams are 5-5 and need one more win to get bowl eligible, but I think the Tar Heels are in the better spot, even on the road. Virginia finally put together a convincing performance against Cal, and congratulations on that, but one good Saturday doesn't erase how rough conference play has been for the Cavaliers. North Carolina hasn't exactly been reliable at home, either. The difference is that the Tar Heels have actually played some of their best football away from Chapel Hill, and I think that travels to Charlottesville. North Carolina is 3-1 in true road games, with wins at Pitt, Duke and UConn. The Pitt and Duke wins came by four points apiece, and the Tar Heels followed them with a 38-21 victory at UConn. That's not a murderer's row, but winning three straight road games is hard to dismiss when we're talking about a matchup priced essentially as a toss-up. Compare that with North Carolina's recent home form: losses to Syracuse, Miami and Louisville in three of its last four games. The results haven't always been pretty, but the road version of this team has been more dependable. Virginia's 36-7 win over Cal looks great on the scoreboard, although it's worth remembering that two of the Cavaliers' touchdowns came on interception returns. That was a much-needed response after losing three straight to SMU, Duke and Wake Forest, including a 51-7 beating at Wake. I've been waiting for Virginia's veteran offensive line to become a consistent strength, but it hasn't happened. The Cavaliers have struggled to protect Beau Pribula and are converting only about 32 percent of third downs. That's a major problem against a North Carolina defense that just showed it can make a good offense work. The Tar Heels lost 16-14 to Louisville last week, but I thought the defense deserved a lot more credit than the final result suggests. Louisville came in averaging more than 40 points and nearly eight yards per play. North Carolina held the Cardinals to 302 yards, just 4.7 per play, and only one gain of more than 20 yards. Derek McDonald has been all over the field with 101 tackles on the season. If that defense shows up again, Virginia isn't suddenly going to find easy yards just because it's playing its home finale. There is one legitimate concern for North Carolina, and that's the quarterback situation. Billy Edwards Jr. left the Louisville game injured and was listed as questionable, while freshman Travis Burgess came in and showed some mobility but also threw an interception. I'm not going to pretend that uncertainty doesn't matter. Still, Virginia has been vulnerable to mobile quarterbacks, and Burgess at least gives the Tar Heels a different way to move the chains if he's needed. North Carolina is also converting around 46 percent of its third downs, compared with Virginia's much lower rate, which is a meaningful difference in a game where possessions could be limited. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium, and this is Senior Day, so the Cavaliers absolutely have a home-field argument. Pribula can hurt opponents with his legs, too, and Virginia's plus-six turnover margin is better than North Carolina's minus-three. Those are real reasons this isn't a slam dunk. But the Cavaliers have struggled to finish drives, scoring on roughly 73 percent of their red-zone trips, while North Carolina has converted better than 90 percent of its opportunities. With neither offense consistently explosive, missed chances inside the twenty could matter as much as the occasional big play. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: North Carolina +1.5 Need More? North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury
away.blurb: A potential two-month recovery timeline could put Avdalas in position to return around January, although North Carolina has not announced a specific return date. North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. His absence will be an early test for Malone and the Tar Heels as they attempt to maintain momentum and navigate the opening portion of their ACC schedule without one of their key offseason additions. home.headline: Who is UNC football’s starting QB vs. Virginia? Billy Edwards Jr. injury update
home.blurb: But at the start of the Tar Heels’ first drive with 11:54 left in the first quarter, it was freshman quarterback Travis Burgess that took the field to lead the offense. Starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. was listed as a game-time decision ahead of UNC’s matchup with the Cavaliers in Charlottesville, Virginia. Edwards was injured in North Carolina’s 16-14 loss to Louisville on Nov. 14 at Kenan Memorial Stadium, and was replaced by freshman Travis Burgess. He was listed as questionable on every previous injury report for the Tar Heels this week, yet was taking first-team reps pregame and exited the tunnel in uniform before the game. But instead of testing Edwards, Burgess got his first-career start. In addition to Edwards’ status, the Tar Heels listed defensive lineman Melkart Abou Jaoude as out and defensive back Greg Smith as out for the first half, which a result of his suspension from the NCAA due to his role in a fight that broke out after UNC’s loss. Abou Jaoude has been dealing with right-hand injury all season that he sustained in the Tar Heels’ season opener against TCU in Dublin and required surgery after he broke “a few” bones, but he’s been able to play while wearing a club. Billy Edwards Jr. is a gametime decision before UNC's matchup at Virginia. Edwards suffered the injury in UNC's 16-14 loss to Louisville on Nov. 14. Freshman Travis Burgess replaced Edwards after the injury against Louisville. The North Carolina football team’s quarterback situation has been an uncertain storyline all week. And hours — even minutes — before its kick at Virginia, it remained uncertain. UNC coach Bill Belichick didn’t give any indication either way on who would be the Tar Heels’ starter against Virginia, saying that the starter was “getting better” and taking things “day by day” on Monday. Edwards was seen going through normal warmups with the rest of the team at Scott Stadium before the game on Saturday morning. The situation was surrounded with further intrigue throughout the week because of how Burgess played when he entered . After getting sacked with 9:14 left in the third quarter, Edwards stayed on the ground for an extended period before leaving the loss to the Cardinals. The offense was in a tough spot at that point, having been scoreless since its first drive. But amid a strong defensive performance, Burgess’ legs ignited the offense just enough that its score with 3 minutes, 43 seconds to play in the game gave it a chance to win the game in the end. Burgess threw for 59 yards on 6-of-11 passes and did damage in the rushing game with eight rushes for 35 yards, perhaps just a missed 39-yard field goal by kicker Rece Verhoff with 8:50 left in the third quarter away from flipping the narrative of the first game he entered at UNC. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs UCLA
picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs UCLA - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs UCLA ANN ARBOR, MI - OCTOBER 24: Michigan Wolverines quarterbacks Michigan Wolverines quarterback Tommy Carr (14), Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19), Michigan Wolverines quarterback Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi (16) and Michigan Wolverines quarterback Brady Smigiel (17) warm up prior to the Michigan Wolverines versus the Indiana Hoosiers game on Saturday October 24, 2026 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan football season felt over when the Wolverines lost to Michigan State, and that defeat seems to have had a similar impact on the team. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. The Wolverines haven't been shutout at home since 1967, but that could change this weekend. UCLA wins, 17-0 UCLA is great defensively, but the Bruins have only eclipsed 30 points once with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback, so I expect Michigan's defense to keep this one relatively close. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.
