(Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Trevor Woods · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:44 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines are 5-5 and have a really tall task on Saturday at Michigan Stadium when they take on the No. 4 UCLA Bruins. The Bruins are 10-0 for the first time since 1998 and have had a remarkable season to this point under head coach Bob Chesney, who is in his first season with the program. While Michigan and UCLA have had seasons that are vastly different, betting odds seem to feel that this game could be closer than perceived. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Michigan is a 3.5-point underdog against UCLA, with the over/under set at 38.5 points. This is a dangerous spread for anyone betting on Michigan — the Wolverines are just 3-7 against the spread this season. Michigan was a 9.5-point underdog against Oregon last week and went on to lose 31-7. UCLA hasn't had the toughest schedule, but Michigan's offense is one of the worst in the nation, and it's yet another week of head coach Kyle Whittingham saying that it will be an open quarterback competition ahead of the game between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood. The betting odds must feel a West Coast team traveling to Ann Arbor in November could prove to be difficult, but the forecast on game day is currently showing it's going to be 63 degrees out — which is abnormally warm for Michigan this time of year. Then there's the tale of two coaches. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney could win coach of the year, while Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham could be one-and-done. There's every reason to believe UCLA will cover in this one.

picks.headline: UCLA vs Michigan Prediction: One Bruin Win Away From The Big Ten Championship
picks.blurb: UCLA vs Michigan Prediction: One Bruin Win Away From The Big Ten Championship - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates UCLA vs Michigan Prediction: One Bruin Win Away From The Big Ten Championship Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:30 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads UCLA got to the 2011 and 2012 Pac-12 Championship games, and lost them both. The football program's last title was the 1998 Pac-10 Championship, won in the regular season. Now, in just its third year as a Big Ten school, UCLA can go to the Big Ten Championship game with one more win in its last two games. Michigan is looking for anything positive at this point. The season crashed through the floor, going 2-5 in Big Ten play – losing to Oregon and Michigan State by a combined score of 46-13 – and now it needs a win in the last two games just to go to a bowl game. UCLA vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan closes with a bang: losing to Oregon 31-7 last week in Eugene, hosting UCLA this week, and finishing with the showdown against Ohio State in Columbus. UCLA closes at USC next week. It won't need the win if it can beat the Wolverines, but obviously, it's the rivalry game the Bruins want. The two teams haven't played since 2000, a 23-20 UCLA win. Starting in 1956 with a 42-13 win, UCLA is 8-3 in the series. How To Watch UCLA vs Michigan Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 250 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why UCLA Will Win Michigan doesn't do that whole scoring thing the kids are all into now. It was bad, there was a false ray of hope when Tommy Carr had a terrific day against a miserable Rutgers defense, and then everything got exponentially worse against Michigan State and Oregon. The Wolverines averaged 301 yards per game – 131st in the nation – and can't score even when they get into the red zone. But that's not the real problem. Michigan has turned it over multiple times in every game except for the wins over Oklahoma and Rutgers, and gave it away once in the loss to Iowa. It turned it over 13 times in the last six games. UCLA is No. 1 in the nation with 30 takeaways. Why Michigan Will Win UCLA isn't the type of team that wings the ball all over the yard. It's a tough, hard-nosed team, but it's not going to run away and hide with a big offensive explosion. The Bruins will play exactly the way Michigan wants. UCLA will need to run the ball, keep the tempo low, and rely on the lines – fine with the Wolverines. This is where the Wolverines can play it tough on the lines, work the field position battle, and try to keep this tight into the final few minutes. Despite the issues over the rough run, the defense is still among the ten best in America. UCLA vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines UCLA will have to work for it, but the defense will come up with the stop it needs late against the punchless Michigan offense. The Wolverines will come out fired up and cranked for the moment, marching down the field with a stunningly crisp opening scoring drive. But UCLA doesn't panic. The Bruin defense will be a rock on third downs, the offense will take the field goals and points when they're available, and Michigan's offense won't be able to take care of its opportunities to pull off the upset. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Look, in at least one way, first-year Michigan football coach Kyle Whittingham delivered exactly what he promised, way back in July. "I can't predict, you know, how good we can be or where we'll end up, but I can say if we're playing meaningful games in November, then that's probably for us a successful season and a chance to have something to build on," Whittingham told reporters at Big Ten media days . (L to R) Michigan State head coach Pat Fitzgerald and Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham talk midfield before their teams game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. OK, OK, half-delivered. Few would say this season has been successful for the Wolverines … but their game against UCLA on Saturday (3:30 p.m., CBS) is certainly meaningful … for the Bruins , that is. A victory over U-M would give UCLA the first 11-win season in program history, as well as clinch a berth in the final Big Ten championship game next month in Indianapolis. On the other hand, a win by U-M would give the Wolverines a bowl berth and the more valuable prize of extra practice days in December. Can U-M pull off the upset (a mild one, at least, as somehow the No. 4 team in the country is merely a 3½-point favorite) and reach the postseason in its home finale? Five Free Press sports writers have some thoughts. Michigan players and coaches say the goal this week is to send the seniors out the right way − with a win. Linebacker Chase Taylor called the chance to face a 10-0 team "motivating" and said "if we want to show the world and stop all the people from talking, then this is how we can do it." The line suggests this game will be closer than the records say it would be, but given Michigan's struggles in scoring, it's hard to see the Wolverines getting enough points for the upset. The defense keeps it close, but like so often this year, it's not enough. The pick: UCLA 16, U-M 10. Carlos Monarrez Fourth-ranked UCLA is undefeated. Michigan is ... not . The Wolverines' only hope is that the Bruins, who beat Illinois last week in front of 45,800 "fans" last week at the half-empty Rose Bowl, will get confused by playing in front of so many fans at the Big House. If Kyle Whittingham has any hope of saving his job, he'll have to get his offense going against the UCLA's fourth-ranked defense. Not happening. The pick: UCLA 33, U-M 12. Kyle Whittingham's first season in Ann Arbor has been a massive disappointment, and it's uncertain if he will get another. Michigan fans are pining for the man who will stand across the field from Whittingham. Bob Chesney has guided the Bruins to an improbable 10-0 start and top-five ranking. Against the Wolverines, he will guide UCLA to its 11 th win and make the home crowd at the Big House want him even more. The pick: UCLA 23, U-M 17. What's the old saying? When you have two quarterbacks, a new AD, a new president, a disappointing season, a first-year coach who hasn't connected with the fanbase (or more importantly, won in any notable fashion) and you are facing an undefeated team in the Big House – you got a whole bunch of trouble brewing. But alas, here comes UCLA coach Bob Chesney to show how you can turn around a program quickly. And yes, he would be one of my first calls: Make him say no. The pick: UCLA 20, U-M 14. Shawn Windsor Even a win probably wouldn't be enough to save Whittingham's job, unless he beats Ohio State, and even then, that's hard to see in the wake of Trev Alberts' hiring as Michigan's new athletic director this week. The new AD is here to change it up. It's not Whittingham's fault that JJ Buchanan, the team's best receiver, got hurt at Oregon and will miss the rest of the season. It is his fault, however, that the offense has been otherwise ... not good . And won't be again against UCLA. The pick: UCLA 16, U-M 6. away.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. Brady Norton is questionable, too, and the Wolverines could opt to play both Manuel Beigel and Marky Walbridge once again this weekend. After back-to-back losses to Michigan State and Oregon, the Wolverines are looking to get back in the win column. In fact, Michigan needs one more win in the last two weeks in order to go bowling. The Wolverines haven't missed a bowl game since 2014, the final year of Brady Hoke in Ann Arbor. If Michigan is going to gain bowl eligibility this weekend, the Wolverines are going to have to earn it. Michigan will host UCLA, which hasn't lost a game all year. The Bruins are one of the most surprising teams in college football. Despite losing Nico Iamaleava for the season, Bob Chesney has turned to his backup quarterback, but it's only resulted in success. If the Wolverines are going to beat UCLA , it's going to have to get the job done without a few players. Here's how Michigan's initial availability report looks heading into the Wolverines' Week 12 game against UCLA. More concern regarding the offense Michigan will also rely on Travis Johnson and Salesi Moa moving forward. Whittingham noted that tight end Mason Bonner could also see some play. It's also concerning to see Rod Moore on the list after he played last weekend against Oregon. The Wolverines' secondary got beat a few times against Oregon, and having a veteran back there like Moore would only help against UCLA. away.headline: Game Thread: Michigan football hosts No. 4 UCLA on Senior Day
away.blurb: Michigan football returns to Ann Arbor for its final home game of the season Saturday afternoon, welcoming No. 4 UCLA for a matchup between two programs heading in completely opposite directions. The Wolverines (5-5, 2-5 Big Ten) are coming off another disappointing performance, falling 31-7 to Oregon last weekend. The loss marked Michigan’s third straight defeat and left head coach Kyle Whittingham’s squad still needing one more victory to be bowl eligible. Unfortunately, things won’t get any easier against the Bruins. UCLA (10-0, 7-0 Big Ten) has been one of college football’s biggest surprises this season, going from three wins in 2025 to an undefeated record under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins enter Saturday’s contest with an opportunity to secure their first 11-win season in program history and clinch a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. The Wolverines will certainly have their hands full against a UCLA defense that leads the nation with 30 takeaways, including 20 interceptions. That’s particularly concerning for a Michigan offense that has committed 19 turnovers this season. On the other side, the Bruins have found success behind quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who has helped keep UCLA undefeated since taking over for the injured Nico Iamaleava. Former Michigan wide receiver Semaj Morgan also returns to Ann Arbor, leading the Bruins with 41 receptions for 525 yards. Michigan’s defense has been one of the few consistent bright spots this season, ranking ninth nationally in total defense and allowing just 17.7 points per game. The Wolverines will need another strong performance from that unit if they hope to slow down UCLA and give their struggling offense a chance. Today’s Question: Can Michigan get anything going offensively? Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood both saw action against Oregon, with neither able to provide much of a spark offensively. Whittingham opened the quarterback competition again this week, leaving the starting job undecided heading into Saturday’s matchup. Interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding will also be looking for a better showing in his second game calling plays. Michigan managed just seven points against the Ducks, although freshman running back Savion Hiter provided one of the few bright spots, rushing for a career-high 107 yards, including a 70-yard touchdown. Interestingly enough, ESPN’s matchup predictor gives the Wolverines a 46.9 percent chance of stealing this one, but will Michigan’s offense realistically give them a chance on Saturday? Let us know what you think in the comments below!

away.headline: UCLA football injury report: Jalen Woods, Riley Robell questionable for Michigan game
away.blurb: The first availability report of the week ahead of UCLA's Week 12 matchup at Michigan came out Wednesday. Two key UCLA players will be questionable for this week's game at Michigan. Both linebacker Jalen Woods and center Riley Robell are questionable to play this weekend, according to the initial Big Ten availability report that was released Wednesday. Woods got hurt midway through UCLA's win over Illinois last week and didn't return. UCLA got good news on Woods' MRI, Bob Chesney said Monday, but the injury was still significant enough for the linebacker to not return last week. Robell suffered a lower body injury against Minnesota two weeks ago, which kept him out last week and led the UCLA coaches to move guard Carter Sweazie to center. Additionally, starting right tackle Hall Schmidt , reserve wide receivers Jalen Saint Paul and Shane Rosenthal, reserve defensive linemen Ashton Sanders and reserve defensive end Ryan McCulloch have all been ruled out for the Michigan game. Michigan will be down its two starting offensive tackles against UCLA in Andrew Sprague and Blake Frazier. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for LSU vs. Tennessee
picks.blurb: LSU heads to Knoxville on Saturday looking to bounce back from consecutive losses against Alabama and Texas. At 6-4, the Tigers have fallen short of preseason expectations, but they still have an opportunity to make a statement against one of the SEC's top teams. No. 9 Tennessee enters the matchup at 8-2 with College Football Playoff aspirations still alive. With both teams fighting for different reasons, Saturday's contest could deliver some unexpected results. Here are three bold predictions for LSU's matchup against Tennessee. Sam Leavitt throws for 300 yards and 3 touchdowns Tennessee boasts one of the SEC's strongest passing defenses , but that will not stop Sam Leavitt from producing one of his best performances of the season. Leavitt leads the conference with 279.7 passing yards per game, although his league-high 12 interceptions have created problems for LSU's offense. Three of those came against Texas last weekend, contributing to the Tigers' narrow 22-21 defeat. Still, Leavitt has shown flashes of the quarterback LSU expected when it landed him through the transfer portal. Lane Kiffin will need to establish an aggressive passing attack, particularly against a Tennessee defense capable of making opponents uncomfortable. Expect Leavitt to spread the ball around, take several shots downfield and for the offense to have a huge sense of urgency. LSU holds DeSean Bishop under 100 rushing yards Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop stands alongside the SEC's most productive offensive players this season, entering Saturday with 1,163 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. Slowing him down will be essential for an LSU defense already dealing with injuries, including the absence of linebacker Whit Weeks and safety Dashawn Spears. The Tigers have demonstrated their ability to disrupt opposing offenses, ranked as the #1 Sack leader with 40, (Though Tennessee is #2 with 39). That aggressiveness could become particularly valuable against a Tennessee team dealing with uncertainty surrounding quarterback George MacIntyre's health. With leading receiver Mike Matthews sidelined, Tennessee could become increasingly dependent on Bishop to sustain drives. LSU should respond by loading the box and forcing the Volunteers to generate production through the air. Bishop will still make plays, but LSU's defensive front will prevent him from taking over the game. Prediction: Bishop finishes with 78 rushing yards and no touchdowns. LSU hands Tennessee its third loss of the season Despite LSU's disappointing record, Saturday presents an opportunity to spoil Tennessee's playoff hopes and secure a signature victory in Kiffin's first season. The Tigers have struggled to finish close games, most recently surrendering a late lead against Texas. However, LSU has remained competitive against several of the nation's strongest programs, suggesting its record does not fully reflect its potential. Tennessee enters with considerably more at stake, and that pressure could work against the Volunteers if LSU keeps the contest close. Expect an aggressive offensive approach from Kiffin, a timely defensive takeaway and a late scoring drive to decide the outcome. Prediction: LSU defeats Tennessee 27-24 on a game-winning field goal . Pictured: Dilin Jones (left) and DeSean Bishop (right) While winning the National Championship would have been a lofty goal to achieve in year 1, many in Baton Rouge at least expected Lane Kiffin to get LSU into the College Football Playoff after taking Ole Miss to the CFP last season and bringing in a heralded transfer class. With a fourth loss last week to Texas, the Tigers' CFP chances are over this season. However, Kiffin gets a shot to possibly deny another of his former schools a CFP berth this week. Kiffin is still not particularly well liked in Knoxville after bolting to USC after one season. However, Josh Heupel got the Volunteers in the CFP in 2024 and is seeking his second berth in three years. The Volunteers are two wins from solidifying a spot as they sit at No. 9 in the CFP rankings and will likely be a double-digit favorite at Vanderbilt next week. Running back DeSean Bishop and an elite defense have led the way this season. Bishop is one of the running backs I will be focusing on in this game. So, here are my Tennessee vs. LSU picks and college football parlay for college football Week 12 on Saturday, November 21. Tennessee vs. LSU Picks Dilin Jones 60+ Alt Rushing Yards DeSean Bishop Anytime Touchdown Parlay Odds: +386 via FanDuel Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Tennessee vs. LSU Odds, Lines 45.5 -110o / -110u Tennessee Odds LSU Player Prop: Dilin Jones 60+ Alt Rushing Yards After transferring in from Hawaii , Jackson Harris has emerged as the star of LSU's offense with 80 receiving yards in five of his last nine games. However, as of Thursday's availability report, Harris was still listed as questionable. Even if Harris does go this week, it may be a week where the Tigers lean on the ground game more. Tennessee is 34th in Passing Success Rate Allowed and leads the FBS in Passing Explosiveness Allowed. However, it is 43rd in Rushing Success Rate allowed and 68th in Rushing Explosiveness Allowed. The Volunteers are allowing 120.5 rushing yards per game and are 59th with 3.9 yards per carry allowed. Enter Dilin Jones, who is the SEC's fourth-leading rusher. The Wisconsin transfer has run for 838 yards and eight touchdown s this season, but his consistency and the trust that Kiffin has in him really stand out. Jones has had at least 14 carries and at least 50 yards in every game, averaging 18.5 carries and 83.8 yards per game. He has run for 60 yards in eight of 10 games this season. If he gets 14 carries once again, he would be on pace for 63 rushing yards based on 4,5 YPC average this season. Tennessee Player Prop: DeSean Bishop Anytime Touchdown While Jones is fourth in the SEC in rushing yards, the Volunteers have the SEC's leading rusher in Bishop. The junior leads the SEC with 1,163 rushing yards and is second with 13 rushing touchdowns. As a result, Bishop's yards line is nearly 50 yards higher than Jones's, even though he has the more difficult matchup. LSU is ninth in the FBS rushing yards allowed per game (86.1), fifth in yards per carry allowed (2.7), and 28th in Rushing Success Rate allowed. However, the Tigers have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns this season. Bishop seems to score every week — actually in eight of 10 games this season. He did not find the end zone against Texas A&M last week, snapping a five-game streak with a touchdown. He will look to start a new streak at home and has scored in 17 of his last 20 games dating back to last season. While I love the 85% hit rate, I am also targeting Bishop to score instead of his yards because Sam Leavitt has thrown 12 interceptions this season, including seven against ranked teams. If the Volunteers intercept Leavitt this week, they may set up a short field for a Bishop red zone touchdown. If you don't believe me, take a look at some of the high-profile matchups for both teams this season and the final score. vs. Texas A&M 35-6 (W) vs. Alabama 31-13 (L) vs. Texas 22-21 (L) vs. Texas 20-17 (L) vs. Alabama 26-10 (W) vs. Kentucky 34-6 (W) All six of those games finished under 46 points. In total, Tennessee is 8-2 to the under while LSU is 5-5 this season. This week's matchup pits two of the FBS ' top-20 scoring defenses and the two teams are allowing 32.4 points per game combined. The two teams are also the top two in the FBS in forcing three-and-outs and sack rate . Additionally, this game may have even less fireworks because LSU may be without Harris and Tennessee will be without leading receiver Mikey Matthews, which will not help a developing Tennessee passing game. All signs point to an under in this matchup and we get on the right side of the key number of 45 as well as a negative correlation odds boost from the two rushing props. away.blurb: Junior Jackson Harris has been listed as a "game-time decision" on the Tigers' final injury report released 90 minutes before kickoff Saturday. He was listed as questionable Friday night. Fellow receivers Winston Watkins Jr. and Jayce Brown have been ruled out for the Tigers (6-4, 3-4 SEC), who are looking to snap a two-game losing streak against a Vols team in position to make the College Football Playoff. He opened the season as one of LSU's starting wide outs but faded back to a smaller role as other receivers like Eugene Wilson III and Jackson Harris emerged out of the pack. LSU will also be without star linebacker Whit Weeks, freshmen defensive linemen Trenton Henderson and Richard Anderson, as well as the guys who have been ruled out for the remainder of the year in safety Dashawn Spears, receiver Phillip Wright III and linebacker Charles Ross II. KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — LSU football could be without its top pass catcher against No. 9 Tennessee inside Neyland Stadium Saturday, Nov. 21. If Harris can't go for LSU (6-4, 3-4 SEC), it'll be a major blow for an offense that has struggled to score points the last two games. This is the first time this season Watkins has missed a game in 2026. Through nine games, Watkins has amassed 41 catches for 517 yards with two touchdowns. picks.blurb: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL SMU SPORTS NEWS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET SI.COM MUSTANGS FB MEN'S BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM MISTANGS BB DALLAS — The SMU Mustangs (7-3, 5-3 ACC) face one of their toughest road trips of the season this weekend. The Mustangs will travel to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) Saturday night at the historic Notre Dame Stadium. The Mustangs haven’t traveled to South Bend since the late 1980s. SMU holds a 1-6 record against the Fighting Irish on the road. Notre Dame leads the all-time series 10-3 overall. SMU faces a tall task after being routed in their first ACC loss at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in over three years. The Mustangs were drilled by No. 13 Wake Forest 49-7 last week. The Demon Deacons outgained SMU 535-275 while holding the Mustangs to 209 passing yards and 69 total rushing yards. As a result, SMU's chances of heading to Charlotte for the ACC championship game and a potential shot at the College Football Playoff have grown slimmer. SMU Head Football Coach Rhett Lashlee spoke during this week's media availability on his team’s performance last week and the challenge that this week presented to bounce back. “Life’s about opportunities, we had one last week we didn't take advantage of it. We have done a good job of taking advantage of our opportunities here. We did not put our best foot forward last week,” said Lashlee during Tuesday’s media availability. “Sometimes when that happens if we were playing someone that we were expected to beat or what not. I don’t know what you gain from that, but having the opportunity to go on the road against an elite opponent we know it's going to take our very best to beat regardless of what happened last week. I like that it's a great opportunity, a great challenge, and we get to see what we are made of and how we respond to that opportunity.” Notre Dame has been a top team in college football this season. After famously being left out of the College Football Playoff last season, Head Football Coach Marcus Freeman and his team have gone to work to ensure the Fighting Irish don’t leave any boxes unchecked for a guaranteed ticket to the postseason. The Irish are 9-1 through 10 games with a staple win over the ACC leader and former No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, atop their season resume. Notre Dame leads the nation in the fewest yards allowed to opposing offenses. While boasting one of the nation's best offenses. Junior quarterback C.J. Carr is top 10 in passing touchdowns this season with 23, while being among the top 25 in total passing yards with 2,385 this season. Carr has been in the Heisman conversation all season in his second season as a starter. He has only been intercepted twice and sacked three times this season. He is coming off a 200-yard performance against Boston College, after throwing for a season-high 319 yards against Miami. The second-year starter has a veteran pair of wide receivers bolstering the passing attack. Senior wide receiver Jordan Faison leads the receiver room with 615 yards on 49 catches with six scores. Not far behind him is junior receiver Micah Gilbert, who has recorded 614 yards on 38 grabs with six of his own scores this season. Fellow senior Jaden Greathouse is also a reliable weapon for Carr this year, securing 25 catches for 354 yards after dealing with injury for most of last season. The multiple weapons for the home team will be a massive test on the SMU’s secondary. Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. After losing both star running backs to the NFL, Notre Dame’s rushing attack has been bolstered by a pair of young stars with only 11 yards separating them. Freshman running back Jonaz Walton leads the team in rushing yards with 655 yards this season, averaging 7.0 yards per carry this season with five scores. The true freshman ran for over 140 yards and a score in Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College last week. Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. is second on the team in rushing yards with 644. The second year back has had more than 120 attempts running the football this season, with a knack for finding the end zone. James Jr. has scored 10 times so far this season, the most on the roster. SMU allowed 286 rushing yards with 6.4 yards per carry against Wake Forest last week. The Mustangs will have one of the most talented backfield duos in the country rushing at them Saturday night. Lashlee went on to describe Notre Dame’s style of play as methodical and patient, yet still able to be explosive. “The way they play allows them to be patient, methodical, and just wear on you,” said Lashlee. “Because of their talent they create explosive plays, but they are not necessarily wired where they have to. They have no problem going on 10, 12, 13 play drives and just wearing on you. So that's what you worry about over the course of the game.” SMU gears up for one of its toughest tests of the season Saturday in a game that has been circled on the calendar since the schedule was released. SMU had its chance last week to all but land a spot in the ACC Championship, but one 49-7 rocking from Wake Forest later, and now it's looking to play spoiler to Notre Dame's season. Notre Dame vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU not only got blown out by Wake Forest, but that was the final home game. The Mustangs close out at Stanford. Notre Dame still has to deal with a road game at Syracuse to close things out. These two haven't played since 1989 – a 59-6 Notre Dame win. The Irish are 10-3 in the series going back to 1930. The offense is terrific, with a great pace and balance that can be impossible to stop when it gets into a rhythm. Notre Dame hasn't faced too many sharp passing teams, but there was a problem against the stronger quarterbacks. BYU's Bear Bachmeier hit 65% of his passes in the 28-24 win, and Miami's Darian Mensah almost pulled the game out of the fire, throwing for 269 yards and three scores. One loss, one close call, and those were the two times the Irish allowed more than 300 total yards. SMU has one of the nation's most efficient passing games for an offense that averages 456 yards per game. Why Notre Dame Will Win How did Wake Forest destroy SMU? It came out roaring, and it was over. The Demon Deacons cranked up the pass rush against a leaky SMU line, and the three takeaways made things ugly. Yes, SMU works with a pace, but when it doesn't work, everything fizzes. But it's about the takeaways. picks.headline: Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions
picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions (Angela Driskell, Irish Breakdown) Bryan Driskell · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame will look to build its College Football Playoff resume when it takes on the 7-3 SMU Mustangs. The Irish fell to 6th in the playoff rankings on Tuesday despite blowing out Boston College by a 41-7 score last weekend. Notre Dame doesn't have a ranked opponent left on the schedule, but the Mustangs will help improve the overall strength of schedule, should the Irish earn a win. Notre Dame makes the playoff if they win out, but a dominant win would be even more helpful. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET Networ k: NBC/Peacock Here are our staff predictions for the game: Prediction : Notre Dame 38, SMU 17 Some of the magnitude of this game was diminished when SMU lost to Wake Forest last weekend in a blowout (49-7). SMU is a much better football team than it showed against the Demon Deacons, and that game reminded me a lot of Notre Dame's loss to Miami in 2017. It was one of those games that just got away from them early, but make no mistake, SMU is a dangerous football team. Notre Dame will need to play at a high level, because I expect SMU to come out looking to make an early statement and bounce back from their bad loss last weekend. The key for Notre Dame will be coming out early and jumping all over the Mustangs. They will need to quickly take away SMU's confidence and not let their potent offense get into any kind of rhythm. That will require the defense to be turned loose and be allowed to attack quarterback Kevin Jennings . If they are allowed to do that, and if the DL handles business, they will force Jennings to make mistakes, and that's how Notre Dame rolls in this game. My prediction is based on SMU being able to make some plays early due to their impressive talent at wide receiver and the fact Jennings is a dangerous player. I expect the Irish defense to quickly get up to speed and slow SMU down over the final two quarters. On the other side of the ball, Notre Dame will look to establish the run game early and get Nolan James Jr . and Jonaz Walton to get going. They will look to soften the Mustangs up and that's when CJ Carr should get rolling and pick the Mustangs apart. If the offensive line handles business the Notre Dame offense should have a big day and the Irish should roll. If Carr gets going early the offense could be extremely difficult to stop in this matchup. Prediction : Notre Dame 41, SMU 13 This is the final of three major tests for the 6th ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish. SMU is coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest at home during their own Senior Day matchup, but don't let that fool you, this is still a talented team making the trip up north. But like a lot of their opponents for the 2026 season, this matchup is more about Notre Dame living up to its potential than it is about facing an opponent that's superior. As it was said best in Wednesday's show, Marcus Freeman needs to know 'what time it is' in college football. SMU is a quality opponent, but not good enough that simply winning the game will boost their resume all on its own. I expect the Fighting Irish offense to come out firing early. Quarterback CJ Carr will hit some big plays early. The biggest question, will Notre Dame keep their foot on the gas after jumping out to an early lead? I think they answer that to a degree, but Freeman needs to learn from the lessons he's experienced in the previous two seasons. I have the Irish winning by 28 on Senior Day. I'm picking Notre Dame to win convincingly against SMU, but this game is about more than simply adding another win to the schedule. With the College Football Playoff committee evaluating every result, the Irish need to make a statement and show that they belong among the nation's elite. Notre Dame cannot afford to play down to its competition or let SMU hang around into the second half. This is an opportunity to dominate on both sides of the football, establish the running game, stretch the field offensively, and demonstrate the kind of physical superiority that separates playoff contenders from everyone else. The Irish need to take care of business, but they also need to make it look impressive. SMU has enough offensive talent, particularly with quarterback Kevin Jennings , to make things interesting if Notre Dame allows it. However, coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs are vulnerable, and Notre Dame needs to take full advantage. I want to see the Irish defense create turnovers, get after Jennings, and keep SMU from finding any offensive rhythm. More importantly, Notre Dame needs to keep its foot on the gas rather than become conservative with a comfortable lead. The committee won't just see another win but it will see how the Irish perform against an opponent they are expected to handle. This is a chance to deliver a dominant performance, build momentum, and send a message that Notre Dame is a legitimate national championship contender. Prediction : Notre Dame 52, SMU 13 Before last weekend, I was going to pick a closer game (something like 38-24), but a combination of both the SMU blowout loss to Wake Forest and Notre Dame's dominant win over Boston College made me reconsider. First, I was pleased that the Irish played the attacking style of defense against Boston College that we saw for the second half of 2025, early in 2026, and then again against Miami. I don't think SMU's offensive line can hold up against the Irish front-seven when they play aggressively. The Mustangs gave up three sacks and six tackles for loss to Wake Forest, and rank 96th in the country in sacks allowed in road games this season. Getting SMU behind the sticks is going to put the onus on Kevin Jennings to make plays. He is really talented, but has a penchant for putting the ball in danger and making a few of those "what is he doing" kind of plays per game. There's a reason that SMU ranks 118th in the country in turnover margin at -6, and Notre Dame ranks 2nd at +16. Also, whether its due to corruption, malice, or just plain incompetence, there are no guarantees for Notre Dame when it comes to the CFP Committee. Marcus Freeman knows that it's not enough to just win these final two games - the Irish need to be dominant if they want to secure a home playoff game. With Wake Forest having such a big win last weekend over SMU - in Dallas no less - I think that will force Freeman and the Irish to keep the pedal down more than would be typical on a Senior Day when the staff typically tries to get all seniors a couple snaps once the game is in hand. Notre Dame's offense should not have much trouble moving the ball against a Mustangs defense that was blitzed by the two best offenses it faced (giving up 488.5 YPG against ranked opponents), and I think the Irish send a message on the scoreboard. Prediction : Notre Dame 35, SMU 10 SMU is a rising program, no question, which was why I was definitely surprised to tune into the game in the second half on Saturday to see such a lopsided score against Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons hammered SMU, leaving them off the scoreboard in the first half and quickly lighting up the scoreboard. While the Mustangs can certainly compete with anybody and Saturday's score was definitely out of character with how their season has gone, I don't think Notre Dame will have much trouble with them, provided they get off to a good start and play disciplined football. It really feels like Mike Denbrock has found his groove, with a great mix of run-and-pass with CJ Carr and Notre Dame's three-headed monster in the backfield: Jonaz Walton , Nolan James Jr. and Aneyas Williams . Give me the Irish.

away.headline: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Junior defensive tackle Francis Brewu is to set to return for Notre Dame football this week against Southern Methodist after missing nearly three full games with a left knee injury. The 6-foot-1, 285-pound Pittsburgh transfer had been listed as questionable on the official injury report since going down seven snaps into the Navy game on Oct. 31 in Foxborough, MA. Fellow defensive tackle Jason Onye, injured five snaps into the Navy game, remains questionable with a right knee injury as of Thursday’s late-week availability update. Return to play: Notre Dame football must work Brauntae Johnson back into game shape Partridge recruited Brewu to Pitt out of Westerville, OH before spending the 2024-25 seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. The reunion has been good for both parties. “We made sure and pointed it out (in film study),” Partridge said of Brewu’s advanced technique against Navy. “That's just an example of how he's playing the game right now. I’m proud of him. I’m happy for him.” This article originally appeared on South Bend Tribune: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU “(Brewu) has played really, really well,” defensive line coach Charlie Partridge said in early November. “I'm proud of his growth. He's had a lot to learn since he's been here. It's a completely different style of defense than Pittsburgh plays, and it was a challenge for him early. “ Brewu averaged 24 defensive snaps through the first seven games, peaking at 35 snaps in the Oct. 17 loss at BYU. His 84.3 overall defensive grade, per Pro Football Focus, is tied for eighth among FBS defensive tackles with at least 175 snaps this season. His 84.5 grade as a run stuffer is seventh. Oregon transfer Tionne Gray (70.1) is tied for 139th overall at defensive tackle, while Armel Mukam (69.1) is tied for 161st. “Because I've known him so long, I was probably harder on him than some of the other guys,” Partridge said. “But I was that way because I want him to be the best version of himself. And to his credit, he weathered that storm and was playing really good football (before the injury).” Brewu averaged 37 defensive snaps across 13 games in 2025 at Pitt with a high of 61 in Week 3 at West Virginia. His overall PFF grade was 78.4, tying him for 17th among the 147 defensive tackles with at least 450 games snaps last year. “He's rushing the passer well, he's playing the run well,” Partridge said. “There was a play against Navy where it was beautiful. He played the cut (block) with two hands, he cleared the cut, and he leapt off the ground to tackle the guy from behind. Not many people are going to put that on their bingo card to say, ‘I'm going to put this on Instagram.’“ Brewu is tied for third on the team with two sacks, and he counts three tackles for loss among his 16 total tackles. Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

away.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. I’m happy for him.” This article originally appeared on South Bend Tribune: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU “(Brewu) has played really, really well,” defensive line coach Charlie Partridge said in early November. “I'm proud of his growth. He's had a lot to learn since he's been here. It's a completely different style of defense than Pittsburgh plays, and it was a challenge for him early. “ Brewu averaged 24 defensive snaps through the first seven games, peaking at 35 snaps in the Oct. 17 loss at BYU. His 84.3 overall defensive grade, per Pro Football Focus, is tied for eighth among FBS defensive tackles with at least 175 snaps this season. His 84.5 grade as a run stuffer is seventh. Oregon transfer Tionne Gray (70.1) is tied for 139th overall at defensive tackle, while Armel Mukam (69.1) is tied for 161st. “Because I've known him so long, I was probably harder on him than some of the other guys,” Partridge said. “But I was that way because I want him to be the best version of himself. And to his credit, he weathered that storm and was playing really good football (before the injury).” Brewu averaged 37 defensive snaps across 13 games in 2025 at Pitt with a high of 61 in Week 3 at West Virginia. His overall PFF grade was 78.4, tying him for 17th among the 147 defensive tackles with at least 450 games snaps last year. “He's rushing the passer well, he's playing the run well,” Partridge said. “There was a play against Navy where it was beautiful. He played the cut (block) with two hands, he cleared the cut, and he leapt off the ground to tackle the guy from behind. Not many people are going to put that on their bingo card to say, ‘I'm going to put this on Instagram.’“ Brewu is tied for third on the team with two sacks, and he counts three tackles for loss among his 16 total tackles. picks.blurb: Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Sat, November 21, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is facing their final road trip of the season as they travel to CoMo to face off against the Missouri Tigers . We have previewed the explosive Missouri offense and the Tigers' defense that has playmakers at every level. We also detailed the path to victory for the Wildcats to end this two game skid. This is an incredibly intriguing matchup as these are very similar teams in terms of talent and features two teams that have their backs against the wall following back-to-back losses. As we mentioned this week, Kentucky's offensive line is truly the key to this football team and a unit that has to get back to playing at a high level. This offensive line was rewarded for their play that led the Cats to a 7-1 start, which allowed them to be listed as semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. Over the last two weeks and specifically last week against Florida, they have not lived up to those honors. If Kentucky continues to play like that up front, they are in a very realistic danger of closing out the season on a four game losing streak. The offensive line was the position group Will Stein and his staff invested the most in overall for year one of this new regime, and it is fair to say by doing so they sacrificed other position groups like wide receiver. Kentucky needs the offensive line to be the best position group on the football field, and through eight weeks of the season they were consistently doing so. Expect an incredible effort from this group on Saturday night, they need to give Kenny Minchey time in the pocket and create displacement in the run game. This is where the game is won and lost as we saw last week against the Gators. Another key area is turnovers, which is an area that Kentucky was thriving in through the first eight weeks of the season. Over the last two weeks, the Wildcats have forced zero turnovers on defense and it has led to them being -4 in the turnover margin in those two losses. Slot corner Aaron Gates dropped an interception against Florida that could have swung the momentum of the game. Luckily, they could have those similar opportunities arise against Missouri. Per Clark Brooks, who does his own charting of all SEC teams on secstatcat.com, Austin Simmons has thrown the most passes this season that could have been intercepted. Simmons has faced good turnover luck, as he has just three interceptions on the season. If you look at the trend of Kentucky's wins versus losses in conference matchups, the Wildcats are facing well over 30 pass attempts per games in their five wins while facing just 20 pass attempts per game in their three losses. This could play out in the Wildcats favor, Missouri puts the ball in the hands of their quarterback as Simmons is averaging 30 pass attempts per game on the season. This game will fall on three areas in my opinion: which team wins the line of scrimmage, which team can create turnovers and which team simply wants the win more. This is a true coin flip game, Missouri is much more talented than their record shows. The Tigers had to face a Mississippi State team on the road against a healthy Kamario Taylor, an Ole Miss team that had superstar running back Kewan Lacy and just suffered back-to-back losses to Texas and Georgia. I have had a hard time deciding who wins this game because I really think these teams matchup evenly, but I ultimately think Missouri gets the win at home in an extremely hard fought game. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction Dylan Ballard · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 11:05 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That's a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn't sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there's still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein's first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers' playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it "not a good plan offensively or defensively," and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. picks.headline: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back?
picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. picks.blurb: Stanford vs California Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks - Pick Dawgz Pick Dawgz Stanford vs California Prediction 11/21/2026 Today’s College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo 2 days ago Nov 14, 2026; Blacksburg, Virginia, USA; Stanford Cardinal quarterback Davis Warren (8) Stanford Cardinal quarterback Davis Warren looks to pass in the game against the Virginia Tech Hokies at Lane Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brian Bishop-Imagn Images Stanford Cardinal California Golden Bears Over 55.5 (-110) Under 55.5 (-110) California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley, CA Saturday, November 21, 2026 Stanford Cardinal vs Cal Golden Bears Prediction I’m laying the points with Stanford against Cal in the Big Game. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that’s actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they’re playing with the urgency to make that happen. What’s changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he’s averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That’s a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn’t been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford’s recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He’s thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it’s not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That’s been missing from this program for a while. Cal’s offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That’s an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who’s thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don’t have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest , SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That’s not a team that’s simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won’t pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal’s first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn’t suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don’t mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven’t played in Berkeley since October 17, so there’s some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there’s a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: Stanford -2.5

Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. The guys care, I'm a guy who cares. The guys up front care. I know that for sure. We're going to keep doing everything we can for this team." I just try to do my absolute best to put our team in position to win and I haven't done that well enough." The Cardinal will continue to look for quarterback Davis Warren and running back Micah Ford to spearhead the offense against the Golden Bears. Ford is coming off a big workload against the Hokies, rushing for 149 yards on 27 carries and scoring three touchdowns. He's surpassed 100 yards in three of the past four games, leaving him 100 yards short of 1,000 for the season. Stanford safety Charlie Eckhardt will attempt to lead the defense after finishing with two interceptions, a forced fumble, a sack and a season-high 10 tackles against Virginia Tech. "Absolutely relentless effort and attitude all the time," Pritchard said of Eckhardt. "He loves to play football. He loves practicing football. He just exudes everything we want about competition and effort and relentlessness and self-improvement. Chuck embodies so much of what we want to be in this program, and I'm just so happy for him." Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele threw two more interceptions last weekend to give him eight on the season. He was sacked a season-high four times. away.blurb: Friday Update: Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable Skip to main content SI.COM Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. ---FRIDAY UPDATE: Strong was upgraded from questionable to probable on Friday, indicating he is likely to play Saturday. Also, inside linebacker McKinley has been elevated from questionable to probable, so he is likely to be available too. Wide receiver Jordan King has been listed as "out" for Saturday' game. Stanford outside linebacker Ernest Cooper is no longer on the injury report, so apparently he will be available.--- Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Carter Stadium to move within one victory of bowl eligibility. The Horned Frogs get their first shot at that sixth win Saturday, Nov. 21, when undefeated No. 2 Utah comes to Fort Worth for the home finale. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. CT on FOX. The Horned Frogs enter at 5–5 overall and 3–4 in the Big 12. Utah is 10–0 and 7–0 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the upset Saturday, it’s bowl eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs will have one more chance on Thanksgiving at No. 12 Texas Tech. Both opponents held their spots in Tuesday’s College Football Playoff rankings. Utah needed a late touchdown to beat Arizona 40–39 in Tucson last week. Quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four touchdowns and rushed for 100 yards, so the Frogs will have their hands full even when a play breaks down. TCU held Kansas State to 10 points and won the turnover battle 2–0, but the offense still managed just 99 rushing yards and allowed four sacks. As I wrote in my Kansas State report card , the Frogs still have work to do up front. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, finish drives and give the home crowd something to celebrate? Here’s how the KillerFrogs staff sees it. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas, looking for a second consecutive victory after defeating Kansas State 20-10 last weekend. Kickoff is scheduled for 9 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 21, on FOX. My latest college football picks back the Horned Frogs to keep things close in a low-scoring game. TCU is a 7.5-point underdog, with the total set at 46.5. Utah narrowly avoided an upset for the fourth time in five weeks , edging Arizona last weekend in a back-and-forth fourth quarter. Arizona had a 78.5% win probability with 8:06 remaining, marking the third time in four games that Utah's opponent has held a win probability of at least 59.7% in the second half. The Utes have won by more than eight points just once in their last five games. That victory came against a Cincinnati team that has now lost five of its last six. Utah doesn't get any bonus points for taking care of business against a team spiraling toward the end of the season. Don't be surprised if TCU has Utah on upset alert once again in Week 12. Utah vs TCU Over/Under pick: Under 46.5 Playable to 52%. TCU doesn't play in many high-scoring games. Excluding their quasi-scrimmage against Grambling in September, eight of the Horned Frogs' nine other games this season have finished with 44 points or fewer. One reason for the low scores is a defense that Pro Football Focus grades as the 17th-best unit in the country . Another is an offense that struggles to protect the football . The Horned Frogs committed four turnovers against UCF, three against West Virginia, and two against Arizona. All three games ended in one-score losses with limited scoring. Both Utah and TCU have top-50 defenses, according to Pro Football Focus. The Horned Frogs should be able to pressure Devon Dampier , who has completed fewer than 54% of his passes in each of his last two games. Expect points to be at a premium. Utah vs TCU combo Playable to 30%. TCU's strength is its defense. In their three wins against Big 12 opponents in 2026, the Horned Frogs have scored 20, 22, and 17 points . If they are going to keep things competitive against No. 2 Utah in Week 12, it will almost certainly have to be in a low-scoring game. What Rebuild? It has been quite the 2026-27 campaign for the Utes , who enter Saturday’s contest as one of just two undefeated teams in the country and will be well on their way to the College Football Playoff with two more victories. Head coach Morgan Scalley has done a phenomenal job in his first year at the helm after taking over for Kyle Whittingham, who departed for Michigan after 21 seasons with the program. Despite needing to replace star offensive tackles Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu , who were selected in April’s NFL Draft, Scalley did an excellent job bolstering both the offensive and defensive lines with portal talent. While most were expecting a full rebuild, he is now one of just three head coaches to ever start 10-0 in their first season. Senior quarterback Devon Dampier is having a remarkable second season in Salt Lake City, throwing for 2,257 yards and 22 touchdowns. The dynamic dual-threat boasts a top-20 QBR among qualified quarterbacks at 78.7 and has accounted for at least two touchdowns in all 10 games. An elite rushing attack is led by junior tailback Wayshawn Parker , who has rushed for 764 yards and nine touchdowns. The Utes have addressed their significant passing limitations from last year, with senior wideout Braden Pegan emerging as Dampier’s top target with 643 receiving yards. Scalley’s bunch boasts an average scoring margin of nearly 20 points, scoring 37.9 PPG (15th) while allowing just 18.6 PPG (21st). However, Utah is coming off a one-point win over Arizona and could find itself in the midst of another close encounter against TCU . TCU Horned Frogs Betting Preview: At Least There's Defense The Horned Frogs have had a very underwhelming campaign, entering Week 12 at 5-5. Coming off consecutive 9-4 campaigns in 2024 and 2025, head coach Sonny Dykes will surely be looking to post a third straight winning season in his fifth year in Fort Worth. The offense has struggled to find consistency, with senior quarterback Jaden Craig throwing just six touchdowns over his last seven games. The rushing attack has also been far from impressive, with no running back reaching 500 yards. That said, TCU's top three targets have all posted at least 580 receiving yards through 10 games. Plus, senior tight end Kari Ashley , who stands 6-foot-4, has racked up 684 yards and four touchdowns on 57 catches. However, it’s the Frogs’ defense that is the far superior unit, allowing just 15.2 PPG, which ranks 12th nationally. Dykes’ bunch will need a stout defensive effort against one of the country’s highest-scoring offenses to end Utah’s unbeaten run. Utah vs TCU Pick, Betting Analysis While Utah is undoubtedly the far better team, finishing a college football regular season undefeated is an extremely difficult feat that has become even more challenging in recent years. Though I expect the Utes to ultimately prevail, I would not be surprised in the slightest if a desperate TCU team gives them all they can handle in what could be a relatively low-scoring game due to the Frogs’ defensive prowess. From a betting standpoint, I favor backing Utah on the moneyline at -265 rather than laying seven points on the road. The Badgers have absolutely dominated this series since 2004 when Purdue blew a 17-7 fourth-quarter lead at home in a top-10 matchup in which Wisconsin capped off the comeback with a game-winning scoop-and-score in the final minutes. The Boilermakers have lost 18 straight to the Badgers in a streak that includes a 3-15 ATS (16.7%) stretch with an absurd average cover margin of -9.5 points. Over that span, Wisconsin has gone 8-0 SU and ATS in Ross-Ade Stadium. What does that have to do with this year's matchup? Nothing really, but it's still a pretty stunning stretch. I actually think Purdue has a shot at ending the long losing streak on Saturday, as I'm just not sure where Wisconsin is at mentally after blowing a touchdown lead in the final minutes last week at Maryland, which started a backup quarterback. I'm also concerned about where the Badgers are physically. They're beat up along the offensive line and will be missing two of their best defensive backs who suffered injuries last week in College Park. The offense is completely in the tank. Last week, Wisconsin didn't even throw for 100 yards, while its nonexistent run game (112th EPA) averaged just 3.3 yards per carry. The Purdue defense has holes all over, but I'm not sure the Badgers can fully exploit those deficiencies, regardless of who plays quarterback. Hopkins suffered an injury last week, so head coach Luke Fickell may turn back to Joseph, who just doesn't have great receivers to lean on and loves to put the ball in harm's way. It also doesn't help that the offensive line is now nowhere close to 100%. The Wisconsin defense has carried the team for most of the season. The linebackers are particularly stout against the run, but Purdue can't run the ball anyway. So, it will be up to quarterback Ryan Browne to attack this shorthanded Wisconsin secondary that has been much more vulnerable against the pass (71st in Success Rate). This offense has shown flashes this year against top-tier competition. The Boilermakers put up 38 and 36 earlier this season against a pair of potential playoff teams in UCLA and Wake Forest, respectively. I believe they can have enough success through the air to keep this game close throughout. Plus, I have no qualms with fading this anemic Wisconsin offense as a road favorite. Lastly, Purdue (which has played one of the 10 most difficult schedules in the country to date) has quietly had one of the best special teams units in the country to date, while Wisconsin has been merely average in that department. That could ultimately swing the game and/or cover in its favor. Purdue vs. Wisconsin Trend Since 2005, Purdue has been one of the worst teams in the country to back at home. Amazingly, the Boilermakers have gone 48-83-1 ATS (36.6%) over that span vs. FBS foes, failing to cover by nearly four points per game on average. No team in college football has been less profitable in their home building. However, Fickell is just 8-14 ATS (36.4%) as road chalk in league play since becoming a head coach, including a pair of outright losses this season to Maryland and Minnesota. He's also failed to cover by 3.3 points per game on average. Something has to give!
