The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. away.blurb: TCU Faces Major Injury Questions Ahead of Showdown With Utah - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAW TCU Faces Major Injury Questions Ahead of Showdown With Utah (Mike Watters-Imagn Images) Jonah Morgan · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads TCU is preparing for one of its biggest challenges of the season, but the Horned Frogs could have some important injury concerns heading into Saturday's matchup against No. 2 Utah. The Horned Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State, a much-needed win that improved their record to 5-5. However, the victory came with some concerns, particularly surrounding quarterback Jaden Craig, who appeared to be dealing with an ankle injury during the contest. READ MORE: TCU Women's Basketball Lands Two Elite Guards in 2027 Signing Class Dykes acknowledged the importance of Craig's health as TCU prepares to face an undefeated Utah team. Craig completed 20 of 34 passes for 225 yards and a touchdown against Kansas State, but his ability to move around the pocket could be affected if the ankle continues to bother him. The injury also gave sophomore Adam Schobel an opportunity to see additional playing time. With TCU still fighting to secure its postseason position, having a healthy quarterback will be particularly important against Utah's talented defense. And it seems as though Dykes believes that his starting quarterback will be ready to face off with the Utes. "Yeah, I would expect him to play," Dykes said on Tuesday. "He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him to be able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess." READ MORE: TCU gets Primetime FOX Showdown With No. 2 Utah in Fort Worth Another situation worth monitoring involves tight end Ka'Morreun Pimpton. His availability could be significant for an offense that needs as many reliable playmakers as possible against one of the country's top teams. Dykes also has plenty of reasons to be encouraged by what his team showed against Kansas State. The head coach praised the defensive performance, particularly the improvement in stopping the run and limiting explosive plays. TCU held the Wildcats to just 10 points and forced two turnovers. "Sometimes you have to win ugly and that's what we did tonight," Dykes said following the victory. That mentality could be necessary again this weekend. Utah enters the matchup ranked No. 2 nationally with a perfect 10-0 record, making the Utes arguably TCU's toughest remaining opponent. The Horned Frogs have been competitive throughout much of the season, but close losses have prevented them from putting together the record they hoped for. away.headline: Backup QB likely to earn first start for TCU vs. No. 2 Utah after injury update
away.blurb: Senior quarterback Jaden Craig was initially expected to start and was listed as probable in the first Big 12 player availability report on Wednesday night. TCU head coach Sonny Dykes also said Tuesday that he believed Craig would be able to play. But Craig was downgraded to doubtful in Friday’s injury report and seems unlikely to play against the Utes. Craig was hobbled with an ankle injury during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kanas State last Saturday. Saturday night might mark the start of the Adam Schobel era for TCU football. The sophomore quarterback is expected to earn his first start when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4) host No. 2 Utah (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Fox. “I would expect him to play, I think he was a lot better today than he was yesterday,” Dykes said Tuesday. “I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” Schobel has played sparingly this season, with just one passing attempt and 11 yards on four carries. But the former four-star recruit is largely viewed as the quarterback of the future for the program. Schobel got his most extensive action of his career in the win over the Wildcats, mostly on designed quarterback runs, but will now be tasked to lead the Horned Frogs against the highest-ranked opponent to play in the Carter since No. 2 Texas in 1970. "The only way that we could have lost that ball is for Mana to pick it up, possess it and then them strip it from him, so we teach him in that instance, if you see that it's hit the opposing team, go see if you can gain anything out of it, and so it was the right decision by him to do that." Utah's special teams made huge strides in the team's 40-39 win over Arizona. Kicker Dillon Curtis was 2-for-2 on field goals — including a 53-yard make — and 4-for-4 on extra points, including the go-ahead PAT in the fourth quarter. But a muffed punt by Mana Carvalho in the fourth quarter brought down the overall grade for special teams. Carvalho has had a number of close calls this season, and one finally went the wrong way for him against the Wildcats. The Utes, up by five, had just forced an Arizona punt with 10:27 left and were in position to possibly take a two-score lead with a successful offensive drive. Carvalho should have either fair caught the punt or let it go with Dwight Bootle II barreling down on him, but Carvalho tried to field it and muffed it, then got rocked by Bootle and had to be helped off the field and into the medical tent. Utah's defense held strong as Arizona threatened in the red zone on the ensuing drive, forcing a field goal. Those saved four points would prove crucial in a one-point win. "We'll know more by midweek. ... We think he's going to be all right," Scalley said. "You never know with that though. I don't want to paint myself into a corner." Utah knows it has to improve in fielding punts as it hits the most important part of the schedule. Will the Utes make a change? TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah
home.blurb: TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah The TCU Horned Frogs face a massive hurdle ahead of Saturday's showdown against the No. 2 Utah Utes. Starting quarterback Jaden Craig landed on Friday night's Big 12 availability report as doubtful, putting sophomore backup Adam Schobel in line to make his first career start, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. TCU listed Craig as probable earlier in the week before downgrading him Friday night. Losing Craig deals a major blow to a 5-5 Horned Frogs offense chasing bowl eligibility against an undefeated 10-0 Utah squad. The Harvard transfer ranks third in the Big 12 with 266.4 passing yards per game, completing 223 of 344 throws for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions while adding four rushing scores. Against Kansas State last Saturday, Craig went 20-for-34 for 225 yards and a touchdown without throwing a pick. Now, the spotlight shifts to Schobel. The 6-foot-5 former four-star recruit from Columbus, Texas, has seen limited action across three appearances this season. He threw one incomplete pass against the Grambling Tigers in September and logged four carries for 11 yards, including three rushes for three yards against Kansas State. TCU's injury woes extend beyond the quarterback room. The Horned Frogs also ruled out running back G'Ivori Graham and linebacker Keylan Abrams for Saturday's contest in Fort Worth, though defensive tackles Markis Deal and Ansel Din-Mbuh alongside edge rusher Cheta Ofili remain probable. Meanwhile, Utah ruled out safety Marcus Wimberly and listed long snapper Logan Castor as questionable. Throwing a first-time starter against the Big 12's top team is no easy task, but Schobel gets his shot to shock college football under the Fort Worth lights. Oklahoma QB Drew Mestemaker remains questionable for Arizona State clash Allan Binoy, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sat, November 21, 2026 at 6:34 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Craig has battled an ankle injury since TCU's 29-28 loss to the Arizona Wildcats two weeks ago. He played through a noticeable limp during last week's 20-10 win over the Kansas State Wildcats and missed Tuesday's practice, though head coach Sonny Dykes initially expressed optimism that his starter would play.
